note: The protocol conformance cases every SDK must pass (model/PROTOCOL.md section 11). Each harness names a test after the case id, in square brackets, for example `[retry.429-retry-after] …`; scripts/check-conformance.mjs fails a language that skips or fails one. The example cases (cases/examples.json) are checked the same way, as `[example] <id>`.

cases.title: A 429 with Retry-After 2 waits at least 2 s, then succeeds
A 503 with Retry-After 1 waits at least 1 s, then succeeds
A long Retry-After (7 s) is honoured in full
With a budget of 10, two retries on 503 spend it; the next call's 503 fails at once with one request; a failure with no response costs 10
With a budget of 5, a call that succeeds after one retry refunds it, so the next call can retry too
With an empty budget (size 0) the first attempt still goes: a 200 succeeds, and a 503 fails with one request
The idempotency key is generated once and kept across retries
An operation that is not retry-safe (SendMessage) is sent once on a 503
A Retry-After above maxRetryDelay fails at once with the typed error
A list runs to the last page, following nextCursor
Typed events, keep-alive comments ignored, finalMessage() returns the final event's member
A dropped stream resumes with Last-Event-ID, without duplicates
A clean end of stream before the final event also resumes
Resuming an answer that has already finished ends at once: no events, no error, one request
A stream exposes its request id, and every event its SSE event name
message.failed raises the typed error for its status and ends the stream
An unknown event name is skipped
An unknown enum value is kept, not raised
Unknown fields are kept in raw on the output
Unknown fields are kept in raw on nested structures and list items
A 404 is the NotFoundError class with status, code and requestId, with and without X-Amzn-Errortype
A 409 is the ConflictError class
A 412 on a stale ETag is the PreconditionFailedError class
A 429 after retries are exhausted carries retryAfterSeconds
An HTML 404 with no Caitlyn-Request-Id is the NotFoundError class, with status 404, code HTTP_404, no request id and the body kept as text
A 405 with an empty body is the generic error, with status 405, code HTTP_405 and no request id
A text/plain 502 is the generic error, with status 502, code HTTP_502 and the body text, sent once
An HTTP 409 whose problem body says status 400 is the ConflictError class (not ValidationError), with status 409
A 400 VALIDATION_FAILED for a field both set and cleared carries the field errors
A status the operation does not list (a 404 from CreateUpload) is still that status's class; a status no error shape has (405) is the generic error, named CaitlynError
A 404 with a 20 KiB text/html body keeps exactly its first 8 KiB, truncated; a cut never splits a character; a problem body under 8 KiB is kept whole, not truncated
A connection closed before any response, and a refused connection, are the connection error: status 0, code CONNECTION_ERROR, the cause kept
Cancelling a stream closes the connection and raises the language's cancellation error
Cancelling a single call stops it
If-Match is sent from the call option and the new ETag comes back
clear sends only the clear list, and the field is cleared
Exactly the SDK headers: Caitlyn user agent, Caitlyn-Sdk-Model, no AWS headers
Hostile AWS_* variables and ~/.aws files change nothing
An operation newer than the server's Caitlyn-Api-Version fails before anything is sent
Caitlyn-Request-Id and Caitlyn-Api-Version are on successful outputs
A successful call's response metadata gives its HTTP status (200), its request id and, where the language keeps it there, its ETag

caitlyn.call, caitlyn.attempt and caitlyn.upload spans with the shared attributes; a failed call and each failed attempt have a status message, error.type, caitlyn.error.code and an exception event; url.full has no query
One span per call, one child span per attempt, traceparent sent
A workspace hostname resolves to https://<workspace>/api

A workspace given as https://<host>, with or without a trailing slash or in capitals, is the bare hostname; a path, a query string, a fragment, user information or a scheme other than https is refused when the client is created, naming the expected form
A workspace given as a hostname or URL sets the token audience https://<workspace>/api; an endpoint override moves the token request, not the audience
A personal access token is sent as the bearer token, with no token request
One token request serves concurrent calls, with the workspace resource and the scopes
A wrong client secret is a sign-in error with the OAuth code and status
A token is replaced before it expires: a minute early, or halfway through a short life
After a 401 the client signs in again once, and the call succeeds
A second 401 after signing in again is raised, with no third attempt
A refused personal access token fails with 401, without retrying
Authorisation code with PKCE (S256), the workspace resource and the scopes, then calls with the saved token
A callback whose state does not match is refused before any token request
An expired access token is refreshed once with the stored refresh token, and the rotated one saved
A stored access token the server refuses is not sent again: the refresh token replaces it
Five calls sent with a token the server then refuses, whose 401s arrive one after another, cause exactly one refresh, and all succeed
Two clients sharing a token store that offers a lock, each calling with an expired access token, cause exactly one refresh: the second uses the tokens the first saved
A refused refresh token clears the token store and fails with invalid_grant
A call before sign-in fails with sign_in_required and sends nothing
A signed STS GetWebIdentityToken call for the workspace audience, one token exchange, then bearer calls
AWS credentials can come from a provider the caller passes, asked when signing in
Without credentials, awsIam uses AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_REGION
An STS refusal is a sign-in error with the STS code, and nothing is sent
With no AWS credentials anywhere, awsIam fails with aws_identity_failed and sends nothing
A workload identity token is exchanged once; a token for another workspace is refused
A replayed workload identity token is refused
Session mode sends the cookie, Origin on writes, and no Authorization header
